subject: Request: extended proveout (POC) + one-time credits beyond PLG cap
messages:
From: Anna Green <anna@peregrinelabs.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: extended proveout + additional credits

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Peregrine loved Redwood's latency and routing features. Quick ask: our internal stakeholder group needs more runway to validate a regulatory-facing integration. We've burned through the PLG sandbox allotment faster than expected (see attached usage CSV) and the procurement timeline is slipping.

Specific request: a 45-day extension to the POC window and a one-time uplift of 250k tokens (or equivalent credits) so our engineers can complete a second compliance test. Procurement also asked whether we can get any pricing concession if we convert to committed capacity after the POC.

We know this is out of standard self-serve limits — happy to sign a short addendum or put a good-faith deposit on a PO. Can you escalate for exec sign-off? Procurement contact is procurement@peregrinelabs.com.

Thanks,
Anna Green
Head of Integrations, Peregrine Labs
Attachments: peregrine_poc_usage.csv (CSV, 38KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Anna Green <anna@peregrinelabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-28T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended proveout + additional credits

Hi Anna — appreciate the detail and the attach.

Quick reply: we can consider a one-time concession but need Deal Desk / exec approval for anything beyond PLG caps. I'm looping in Laura (Sales Ops) to scope options and Aditya for final authorization.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I will open a formal request with Deal Desk with the usage data and a recommended concession (see below).
- If Peregrine prefers an invoice/PO in advance, we can structure the extension as a short addendum and apply credits after conversion.

Recommended internal option (my thinking):
Option A — conservative: 30-day extension + 150k token credit, no discount.
Option B — conversion-motivated: 45-day extension + 250k token credit + 10% discount on first month of committed capacity if Peregrine signs within 60 days after POC.
Option C — trial bump with deposit: 60-day extension with 200k token credit applied after a $5k good-faith deposit (refundable on signup).

Laura / Aditya — can you review and indicate preferred option or counter? Anna, copying procurement as requested.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-29T08:58:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: extended proveout + additional credits

Thanks for the context, Priyom. Reviewing usage and commercial posture: Peregrine looks like a midmarket-regulated prospect with a realistic chance to convert within 1–3 months if we remove the friction.

My assessment and constraints:
- Anything <= 30 days and <= 150k tokens can be approved by Deal Desk without exec sign-off (we've used this playbook).
- Anything above 150k tokens or longer than 30 days requires senior commercial approval (Aditya / CRO) because it materially impacts our PLG budget and credit allocation.
- We should require a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and a named procurement PO or letter of intent to lower risk.

Recommended framing for exec ask:
- Ask: 45-day extension + 250k token one-time uplift + 10% convert discount (Option B) — because this materially increases chance to close and we have procurement engagement.
- Conditions: signed MAP within 7 days; credits expire on conversion or 90 days after issue; standard data/retention terms only.

I've attached a clean MA draft to use as an addendum (ma_draft_terms.pdf). If Aditya approves Option B I'll send formal Deal Desk packet with redlines and projected unit economics.

Laura Bennett
Head of Deal Desk & Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ma_draft_terms.pdf (PDF, 45KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-30T17:45:00-08:00
Subject: Exec approval request — Peregrine Labs (DEAL-9876) — one-time POC concession

Aditya,

Summary / ask: Peregrine Labs is requesting a 45-day extension to their POC and a one-time uplift of 250k tokens (they're currently at 82% of their PLG allotment). Procurement has signaled intent to move to a paid committed capacity discussion contingent on an additional compliance run. Laura recommends Option B (45d + 250k credits + 10% first-month convert discount) conditioned on a signed MAP and standard data protections.

Why I recommend Option B:
- High likelihood to convert (regulatory use case, strong technical fit).
- Procurement is willing to provide a PO / deposit, shortening procurement lag.
- Net economics: projected ARR if converted = ~$180k over 12 months; downside limited by MAP conditions.

If approved, requested response: please reply with one-line "Approve Option B" or "Deny" so we can move quickly. If you prefer a smaller concession, state "Approve Option A".

Attached: full thread + usage CSV + MA draft.

Thanks for timely review — procurement needs an answer before EOD Friday to avoid a two-week slip.

—Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
